where: Section 1, worked example step 3, exam traps, quiz Q2 and Q3
problem: The stack convention is contradictory. The start move is explicitly said to use top-left transition notation: δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q, S Z₀)} displays as Z₀ S. But then productions push αᴿ, and the trace displays Z₀ b S a after S → aSb. Under top-left transition notation, αᴿ puts the rightmost symbol of α on top, not the leftmost; δ(q,ε,S) = {(q, b S a)} would give display Z₀ a S b and match b first. The example only works if transition strings are read bottom-to-top, which contradicts the start move. Students cannot tell whether to push α or αᴿ.
fix: Use one convention. With top-left transition notation, push α, not αᴿ: δ(q,ε,S) = {(q, a S b)}. Keep the bottom-to-top display Z₀ b S a. Change worked example step 3 to (q, a S b), Q2 to say 'pushing α puts the leftmost symbol of α on top', Q3 to (q, 0S1), and the trap to warn against pushing αᴿ under this convention. Alternatively, use bottom-to-top transition strings throughout, in which case write the start move as δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q, Z₀ S)} and keep αᴿ.

problem: The construction adds a new start symbol S, so the grammar has |Q|²|Γ| + 1 variables, not |Q|²|Γ|. Q8's 48 is only the number of [p A q] variables; the grammar also has S, so the total is 49. A student answering 48 would omit the start symbol.
fix: Say 'the triple construction creates |Q|²|Γ| variables [p A q], plus the new start symbol S, so |Q|²|Γ| + 1 grammar variables.' Change Q8 to 49, or ask explicitly for the number of [p A q] variables only.

problem: The order 'remove useless variables, then ε-productions and unit productions' can leave new useless variables after ε-elimination and unit-elimination. Standard simplification removes ε-productions, then unit productions, then useless symbols.
fix: Reverse the order: eliminate ε-productions, then unit productions, then useless variables. Or repeat useless-variable removal at the end.
